name: Meridians
description: Stones that cannot see a friend die. Place where one of your stones looks, keep every group in sight of another, and take the board away from your opponent.
rules: The board is a hexagon of triangles with no middle point: six intersections along two sides and seven along the other four. Light moves first; stones never move once placed.
Your first stone goes on any empty intersection. Your second must not touch your first.
After that, place a stone on an empty intersection your own stones can see: along one of the board's three straight directions, with no stone of the other colour in between.
A group is your stones that touch one another. A path is a straight line of one or more empty intersections joining two of your groups. A group with no path to another group of yours is dead.

When your turn ends your dead groups are taken off the board — but not before you have had two turns, so your opening stones are safe. A group the opponent killed can be saved by giving it a new path on your next turn.
There is no passing while you have a move. You lose when your turn begins with no stones of yours on the board.
The move limit (1200 plies) ends an unfinished game as a draw.
